highlights: llama.cpp v1.0.0 removes the deprecated public API and makes breaking changes visible through major-version bumps, while DeepSeek exposes the full DeepSeek App experience through its API.
Perplexity released Decider v1.3 (26B) and Decider Flash v1.3 (5B) under Apache 2.0, adding span extraction alongside classification.
Research on decision models and visual generation includes SO-Arena, PhysLoop, Open Vision Banana, and evidence that a poor actor can still teach well.

items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 removes the deprecated public API
items.summary: llama.cpp v1.0.0 removes the deprecated public API and promotes the NextN/speculative API to llama.h, adds OCP FP8 KV caches, a host-memory MoE expert cache, and loading of external PLE shards. The release also adds Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Ripple, xing4 0, drama-3 TTS, and Kimi-K3.1 vision support, hardens llama-server, and adds a /v1/audio/speech endpoint. With breaking public C API changes now tied to major-version bumps, downstream developers can rely on clearer compatibility boundaries.

evidence.quote: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
Today we release libraries v1.0.0 , highlighting our responsibility to those developers.
Moving forward, both llama.cpp and ggml will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps.
As adoption grows, we will be stricter about making those boundaries visible to downstream consumers.
The following rules apply to all ggml-org projects using semantic versioning :
Breaking change to the public C API in ./include
Backward-compatible feature, backend updates, model support, or API addition
Bug fix with no API change
Currently, llama.cpp supports more than 150 architecture variants as well as all mainstream speculative decoding methods.

items.title: DeepSeek exposes the full DeepSeek App through its API
items.summary: The capabilities behind the DeepSeek App, including search, files, links, safety, and voice, are now available through the DeepSeek API, either as built-in features or standalone APIs such as OCR, ASR, and TTS. V4.1-Flash (deepseek-flash) supports these capabilities across Messages, Responses, and Chat Completions, with tool calls and context assembly handled server-side. Extended capabilities incur tool usage fees in addition to standard token charges.

items.title: Perplexity releases Decider v1.3 (26B) and Decider Flash v1.3 (5B)
items.summary: Perplexity released two open-weight classification models under Apache 2.0: pplx-decider-v1.3, fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B, and pplx-decider-flash-v1.3, distilled from the 27B using a KL objective. Both support text and images, and v1.3 adds a locate type that extracts verbatim spans with character offsets and confidence scores for NER, PII detection, and extractive QA. The 26B model needs about 49 GiB of BF16 weights plus working memory and a CUDA GPU, and training used sequences up to 30,720 tokens.

items.title: Claude Blog explains the primitives of always-on agents
items.summary: The guide describes always-on agents as stateful and proactive systems that manage context across sessions and act without direct supervision. It breaks the surrounding architecture into five core primitives: an event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and an outbox. On one long-horizon coding benchmark, Opus 5.5 cost 78% less per solved task than Opus 5, compared with 40% less on typical workloads.

evidence.quote: Building always-on agents Always-on agents run indefinitely, deciding how and when to act across many sessions.
This guide walks through their core primitives and how they fit together.
Always-on agents are stateful and proactive, meaning they manage context across sessions and take actions without direct supervision.
The difference is the surrounding architecture, which is built from primitives that control when the agents wake up, what carries over between runs, and how their work reaches the user.
For example, on one long-horizon coding benchmark , Opus 5.5 cost 78% less per solved task than Opus 5, compared with 40% less on typical workloads.
The core primitives The surrounding architecture of an always-on agent has five core primitives: an event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and an outbox.
The inbox should be the source of truth .
An inbox should only have one active worker at a time .
As a rule of thumb, memory should only hold what the agent can’t look up again.

items.title: Transformers v5.23.0 adds Inkling 2 Small and new model support
items.summary: Release v5.23.0 adds Inkling 2 Small, a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts for 594B total and 17B active parameters. The release also adds the experimental JEV decision head and model support for LFM3, Dots 3, IQuest-Coder-V1, and InternLM3.

evidence.quote: Release v5.23.0

Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages.
Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters.
LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI.
Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers.
Dots 3 Note Preview is a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video, and audio inputs.
IQuest-Coder-V1 is a family of code language models developed by IQuest Lab, available in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants.
InternLM3 is an 8B instruction-tuned language model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory (checkpoint: internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct).
Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend ( #50029 , #50032 , #50309 , #50311 )
Every export now returns an ExportedModel .
You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime.
The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch.

items.title: Cohere completes its AISLE acquisition and acquires cubic
items.summary: Cohere completed the acquisition of AISLE, which builds autonomous systems for vulnerability discovery and remediation, and welcomed the team behind cubic, an AI-powered code review platform. With AISLE and cubic, Cohere has completed four strategic M&A transactions this year, following Aleph Alpha and Reliant AI. The cubic team will establish Cohere's secure coding vertical, with review agents built for enterprise environments including on-premises and air-gapped deployments.

evidence.quote: Today, we're excited to share two important milestones in that journey.
We're pleased to announce the completion of our acquisition of AISLE, the company building autonomous systems for vulnerability discovery and remediation.
We're also welcoming the team behind cubic, one of the leading AI-powered code review platforms, to Cohere.

With AISLE and cubic we’ve completed four strategic M&A transactions this year, following Aleph Alpha , Reliant AI to expand our capabilities across frontier AI, biopharma and healthcare, cybersecurity, and software development.
AISLE’s co-founders are taking leadership roles spanning cybersecurity, corporate security, AI security research and frontier model development.
Ondrej Vlcek will become Senior Vice President, Cohere Cyber, and lead the newly established cybersecurity business.
Jaya Baloo will become Cohere’s Chief Information Security Officer, overseeing security across the company.
Stanislav Fort will become Vice President, AI Security, joining Cohere’s core model research and training efforts while leading AI security research.

The team has built an industry-leading AI-powered code review platform that helps engineering organizations review code, find bugs and vulnerabilities, understand complex codebases, and automatically remediate issues.

Their review agents have consistently ranked among the strongest performers on code review benchmarks and were built for the environments many enterprise customers operate in, including on-premises and air-gapped deployments.

They will establish Cohere's secure coding vertical, helping accelerate the integration of enterprise-grade coding capabilities into our platform while meeting the security, governance, and deployment requirements our customers demand.

items.title: Tontaube V1.1 brings voice cloning and long-form TTS to local hardware
items.summary: TontaubeV1.1 is a multilingual text-to-speech model by Craitech for expressive voice cloning, long-form speech, and low-latency streaming, with first-class support for English and German and additional support for Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, and Portuguese. It clones a voice from 5–60 seconds of clean, single-speaker speech. The default backend runs the 4-bit model, loading in about 4 GiB of GPU memory and peaking at about 6.5 GiB, while the vLLM backend needs at least 24 GiB.

items.title: SO-Arena benchmarks System One models across 11 domains
items.summary: SO-Arena characterizes the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families, combining evidence-grounded evaluation, domain-specific difficulty criteria, and interactive sandbox execution. Reliability is measured through decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition. Evaluations across 21 models show that scaling and additional reasoning help unevenly, and the best-performing System One model ranks only seventh in reliability.

evidence.quote: We introduce SO-Arena , a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families.

For the capability spectrum , SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs ; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria ; and realistic interactive evaluation , where
models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes .

Beyond accuracy, SO-Arena assesses decision reliability through two complementary measures: decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition when no valid option is available.
Evaluations across 21 models reveal that the benefits of scaling and additional reasoning vary substantially across domains.
More importantly, strong overall performance does not necessarily imply reliable decision-making: the best-performing System One model ranks only seventh in reliability.

items.title: Duo v1 introduces a Reciprocal World Model for full-duplex interaction
items.summary: The report introduces the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and presents Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. RWM pairs two capabilities, Intent and Realization, and Duo v1 adds autoregressive modeling for interaction reasoning, chunk-specific conditions and synchronized tokens on a unified timeline, and dual rollout distillation to mitigate distribution shift. Both modules perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling spontaneous conversations and interruptions.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1 , a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time.
The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world.
In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent , which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization , which generates coherent audio-visual behavior.

To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions , rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models .
(2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline .
(3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation , training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization .
Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions.

items.title: PhysLoop uses LLMs to improve video generation physical consistency
items.summary: PhysLoop is a unified harness for physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models, guiding and constraining LLMs through generation, selection, and correction. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. The authors release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair, and they assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.

evidence.quote: We present PhysLoop , a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models .
The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos.
The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair .
By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention.
We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair .
We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark .
Code release is pending company policy review.

items.title: G-STAR compresses discrete autoregressive image tokens by 32× to 64×
items.summary: G-STAR is a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables 32× and even effective 64× compression while preserving reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance, supported by a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. The compressed models compete with leading models across five text-to-image benchmarks. At 1024×1024 resolution, the model delivers a 20× speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200.

items.title: Decision models can teach well even when they act poorly
items.summary: The study compares three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and uses JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a required subgoal by an easier one, while as judges of full trajectories they credit steps toward that subgoal. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop.

evidence.quote: Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents Published on Nov 12 · Submitted by wangzixuan on Nov 13 · Zhejiang University Upvote 29 +21 Authors: Haochen Liu , Qianhao Zhu , Zixuan Wang , Dingming Li , Tongbo Chen , Peng Qiu , Yingqi Qu , Weiming Lu , Jun Xiao , Yongliang Shen Abstract A dec
We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld , and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop .
As actors , all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one.

As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal , and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions.
As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop .
These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate.
Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents.

items.title: Open Vision Banana opens a recipe for generative visual perception
items.summary: Open Vision Banana (OVB) is a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems, covering color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models with 2.1M-3.8M training pairs, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU). Its legend ensembling test-time scaling improves mIoU by up to 8.7 points on Cityscapes and 15.0 points on COCO-Object without retraining.

items.title: SimpleHC simplifies Hyper-Connections with shared memory access
items.summary: A systematic study of Hyper-Connections architectures finds that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates each achieve performance comparable to mHC, and that repeated access to the expanded residual state is a major source of training overhead. The resulting SimpleHC removes residual mixing and uses shared memory access, incurring only 2.4% extra end-to-end training time over a vanilla residual baseline at the largest tested scale. It maintains performance comparable to mHC when scaling from 15B to 30B MoE models.

evidence.quote: ng , Yizhou Chen , Yuliang Liu , Yu Cheng , Junchi Yan Abstract A systematic study of Hyper-Connections architectures identifies the simpler efficient design SimpleHC, which removes residual mixing and uses shared memory access to match mHC performance while adding minimal training overhead and impr

Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models , yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead.
We find that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates form two effective interaction groups: either alone achieves performance comparable to mHC .
We also identify repeated access to the expanded residual state as a major source of training overhead, even without mixing.

These findings lead to SimpleHC , which simplifies the architecture by removing residual mixing and simplifies execution through shared memory access , using the resulting additive structure and shared gate inputs .
SimpleHC incurs only 2.4% extra end-to-end training time over a vanilla residual baseline at the largest tested scale.
It maintains performance comparable to mHC when scaling from 15B to 30B MoE models , exhibits smoother gradient dynamics during standard training, and remains stable under stress.

items.title: Controlled experiments favor dedicated vision capacity for multimodal models
items.summary: The paper disentangles a visual prior, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement through a controlled framework that pretrains all models from scratch on common data and compares them at matched lifetime compute. The visual prior is not necessary, since an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, but dedicated vision capacity matters, as an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding. Vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token.

evidence.quote: , Jakob Verbeek , Saining Xie , Hu Xu Abstract Controlled experiments show that multimodal language models do not need a pretrained vision encoder, but benefit from dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and integrated early rather than before fusion.

Vision encoder s bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining , dedicated vision capacity , and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone ).

We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute .
We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage.
What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity : an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count.
Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion , as vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token .
Overall, our findings favor dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and placed early within it.
